# 'branch onto' with an upstack branch in another worktree
# that conflicts during the move.
# The conflict should be aborted, state updated,
# and the user told to restack from that worktree.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-02-25T16:00:00Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git add init.txt
git commit -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init

# Create a stack: main -> feature1 -> feature2
# feature1 modifies a separate file (no conflict).
# feature2 modifies init.txt (will conflict with main).

git add feature1.txt
gs bc feature1 -m 'feature1'

cp $WORK/extra/feature2-init.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
gs bc feature2 -m 'feature2'

# Create a conflicting change on main.

gs bco main
cp $WORK/extra/main-conflict.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
git commit -m 'Conflict on main'

# Create a separate branch 'target' from main.

git add target.txt
gs bc target -m 'Add target'

# Check out feature2 in another worktree.

gs bco feature1
git worktree add ../wt-feature2 feature2

# Move feature1 onto target.
# feature2 must move onto main, but conflicts.

gs branch onto target

# feature2 should conflict, abort, and warn.

stderr 'Conflict while moving branch in worktree.*branch=feature2'
stderr 'gs branch restack.*branch=feature2'

# feature1 should still move onto target.

stderr 'feature1: moved onto target'

# The other worktree should be clean (rebase aborted).

cd ../wt-feature2
git status --porcelain
stdout '^$'

-- repo/init.txt --
initial content

-- repo/feature1.txt --
feature1 content

-- repo/target.txt --
target content

-- extra/feature2-init.txt --
feature2 content

-- extra/main-conflict.txt --
main conflicting content
